summary: This study investigates the use of metastable atomic layer deposition (MS-ALD) to fabricate complex 3D silica/silver structures using planar silver templates. The process involves the cyclic oxidation and decomposition of silver oxide, leading to the formation of porous silica structures with high surface-to-volume ratios. The study explores the effects of various parameters such as Ag film thickness, number of cycles, and precursor exposure times on the resulting structures.
evidence: The MS-ALD process is based on a silica plasma-enhanced ALD process using tri-(dimethyl)-amino-silane (TDMAS) and oxygen plasma. The substrate temperature was set to 120°C for all experiments. The growth per cycle (GPC) was 1.1 Å per cycle. The process consists of four steps: (1) TDMAS dose, (2) purge of residuals, (3) oxygen plasma dose, and (4) purge of residuals.
